hero.title: SelfHeal Operations & SRE Handbook
hero.subtitle: Field documentation for SRE and DevOps engineers: organization configuration, Kubernetes telemetry setup, and autonomous self-healing policy design.

ch01.desc: SelfHeal is built to bring autonomous infrastructure resilience to SME engineering teams without the steep cost or operational complexity of legacy APM platforms. Before onboarding production workloads, make sure you hold basic administrative permissions on the target Kubernetes cluster.
ch01.prereq1: Kubernetes cluster v1.25+ (EKS, GKE, AKS, K3s, or bare-metal kubeadm).
ch01.prereq2After: CLI installed and configured with cluster-admin access for initial setup.
ch01.noticeBody: The SelfHeal Agent operates strictly over outbound TLS WebSockets. You never need to open inbound firewall ports or expose cluster ingress endpoints publicly.

ch02.desc: An Organization is the top-level tenant isolation unit in SelfHeal. All team members, audit trails, and connected clusters remain strictly isolated inside your organization boundary.

ch05.descBefore: The Agent deploys seamlessly via Helm or standard Kubernetes manifests into a dedicated
ch05.code:
# 1. Add the SelfHeal Helm repository
helm repo add selfheal https://charts.selfheal.infra
helm repo update

# 2. Deploy the agent with your cluster token
helm install selfheal-agent selfheal/k8s-agent \
  --namespace selfheal-system \
  --create-namespace \
  --set clusterToken="sh_live_89f02c91a7e4b" \
  --set clusterName="k8s-prod-us-east-1"
ch05.noticeBody: The Agent binds only a tightly scoped ClusterRole restricting write permissions to pre-approved API groups (Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets). It never has access to cluster Secrets or sensitive ConfigMaps.

ch06.p1: Immediately upon connection, the Agent streams high-frequency resource metrics (CPU, RSS memory, disk I/O, network packet drops) and Kubernetes control-plane events every 10 seconds.

ch07.desc: SelfHeal runs continuous multivariate time-series forecasting models to distinguish brief traffic spikes from sustained degradation curves likely to trigger failures.

items.label: Time-To-Failure (TTF):
items.text: Estimated minutes remaining before an OOMKilled crash or request queue saturation.

items.label: Confidence Score:
items.text: Statistical probability of the predicted failure trajectory (e.g., 96.2%).

items.label: Blast Radius:
items.text: Downstream dependent microservices impacted if remediation is delayed.

ch08.desc: When a pre-incident trajectory is confirmed, SelfHeal opens a structured incident brief. Rather than flooding alert channels with raw noise, the platform surfaces an actionable summary:
ch08.item1Before: Correlated root-cause signals (e.g., Memory leak in
ch08.item2: Ranked remediation strategies with pre-calculated blast radius.
ch08.item3: Simulated dry-run validation results prior to execution.

ch09.desc: Autonomous recovery playbooks are strictly deterministic and leverage native Kubernetes controllers:

items.label: Rolling Pod Restart:
items.text: Gracefully drains and restarts failing pods sequentially without dropping live TCP sessions.

items.label: ReplicaSet Horizontal Scaling:
items.text: Temporarily scales deployment replicas to absorb unexpected traffic surges.

items.label: Automated Rollback:
items.text: Reverts to the last known healthy ReplicaSet revision if crash rates breach policy thresholds.

ch10.desc: Whenever a playbook requires human sign-off, an interactive alert is pushed immediately to designated engineers via the Web UI and Slack/Teams webhooks. Engineers review the full configuration diff and Approve, Reject, or Refine in one click.
